name: AI and Faith homepage: faith-based ethics for artificial intelligence
title: AI and Faith homepage: faith-based ethics for artificial intelligence
answer: This is the homepage of AI and Faith, a pluralist organization that seeks to bring faith-based values into the ethical conversation about artificial intelligence. Its most useful point is that AI issues such as control, privacy, bias and human meaning are deeply moral and, for the 85 percent of the world who claim a religious affiliation, deeply spiritual. The page calls on tech creators, researchers, ethicists and theologians to apply ancient religious wisdom to AI development, and it offers a newsletter and donation route for supporters.

sections.body: AI and Faith publishes this page as its homepage. It is a landing page for the organization, not a report or research paper. It states the group's mission, its focus on bringing the values of the world's major religions into the ethical debate on artificial intelligence, and its aim to encourage, connect and equip tech creators, academic researchers, ethicists, theologians and related professionals. It also invites donations and newsletter signups. The page states no publication date. It was harvested on 2026-09-26.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page says artificial intelligence has transformed human interaction in promising and troubling ways. It lists emerging issues around control and power, privacy, bias and discrimination, economic well-being, and the understanding of what it means to be human. The organization's mission is to equip and encourage people of faith to bring time-tested, faith-based values and wisdom to the ethical AI conversation. It argues that each issue is deeply moral and, for the 85 percent of the world's population who claim a religious affiliation, deeply spiritual. AI and Faith believes the world's religions offer ancient wisdom that should guide AI development and use. It encourages, connects and equips tech creators, academic researchers, ethicists, theologians and related professionals to engage moral and ethical issues around AI and related technologies. Its focus is to bring fundamental values of the world's major religions into the emerging debate on ethical AI development and to apply faith values to essential questions from new forms of intelligence. A quote says the goal is to inject humility and historicity into an industry that has often rejected them both, and calls the project deeply humanistic, bringing faith-based, literary, classical and oral traditions to bear on what may be the most important technological transformation of our time. The page also asks for tax-deductible donations and offers a monthly newsletter roundup on AI, ethics and faith. An unrelated Italian paragraph about website design and mobile games also appears.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives one figure: 85 percent of the world's population claim a religious affiliation. It also states positions: AI issues are deeply moral and spiritual, the world's religions offer ancient wisdom for AI development, and AI and Faith is a pluralist organization. It quotes a goal to inject humility and historicity into an industry that has often rejected them both. It says donations are tax-deductible and a monthly newsletter covers AI, ethics and faith. No other numbers appear.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in churches and faith organisations would use this page to understand how one group frames the field. AI and Faith positions itself as a pluralist organization that connects tech creators, researchers, ethicists and theologians, and it gives a concise rationale for faith involvement: AI ethics is moral and spiritual, and religious traditions offer wisdom for AI development. For churches and faith organizations, the page offers language for why they might join the AI ethics conversation, plus a newsletter and donation route. It does not provide practical guidance, tools or case studies for congregations.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Churches and Faith Organisations

sections.body: This is a homepage, not a report, study or detailed program description. It states no publication date. It does not name specific projects, events, research findings or ethical positions beyond general mission language. It is partly promotional, asking for donations and newsletter signups. The harvested text also contains an unrelated Italian paragraph about website design and mobile games, which does not fit the mission. It does not cover how churches or faith organizations should use AI in worship, pastoral care or administration.
